industryStandard.name: Film Screenplay
industryStandard.description: Industry-standard feature-film screenplay formatting (Final Draft compatible).

oneHourDrama.name: 1-Hour TV Drama
oneHourDrama.description: Single-camera teleplay for hour-long dramas. Same look as a feature screenplay with TV act structure (Teaser, Acts I–V).

multicamSitcom.name: Multi-Cam Sitcom
multicamSitcom.description: Multi-camera teleplay (live-audience sitcoms): double-spaced dialogue, all-caps underlined stage directions, scene character list, scene-per-page.

stagePlay.name: Stage Play
stagePlay.description: Theater script: centered character names, italic parenthetical stage directions, ACT/SCENE structure.

radioPlay.name: Radio Play
radioPlay.description: Audio drama: numbered scenes, SOUND/MUSIC cues, narrator. No camera or visual elements.
radioPlay.tagline: Radio drama / audio play (BBC, podcast fiction)

podcast.name: Podcast
podcast.description: Scripted podcast and audio fiction: every line of dialogue numbered for the recording session, FX and music cues numbered on their own.
podcast.tagline: Scripted podcast / audio fiction, lines numbered for recording

comic.name: Comic Book
comic.description: Comic book and graphic novel full script: pages and panels numbered automatically, captions and balloons lettered 1, 2, 3 down each page.
comic.tagline: Comic book / graphic novel full script, pages and panels numbered

avScript.name: AV Script (Two Column)
avScript.description: Two-column Audio | Video script — commercials, corporate video, documentary. Each row pairs a video shot with its audio.

picker.title: Choose script format
picker.empty: No formats enabled. Open Format → Script Format Preferences to choose at least one.

format.defaultTooltipClear: The New Screenplay picker opens on this format. Click to clear.
format.defaultTooltipSet: Open the New Screenplay picker on this format

conflict.title: Template Conflicts
conflict.intro: Applying {{name}} requires resolving the following conflicts in your document.

disabled.title: Disabled Element Types
disabled.desc: These element types are disabled in the template but exist in your document. Choose a replacement for each.

formatting.title: Formatting Conflicts
formatting.desc: These elements have inline formatting that conflicts with the template's locked rules. Check to strip conflicting marks.

prefs.title: Script Format Preferences
prefs.hintFirstRun: Pick the formats you commonly write in. When you create a new script, OpenDraft will offer just these options. You can change this later from the Format menu.
prefs.hint: Choose which formats appear in the New Screenplay picker. Make one the default and the picker opens on it, ready to accept — the others are still one click away. Select just one format and new scripts use it without prompting at all.
prefs.noneYet: None yet. Format ▸ Formatting Template… is where you create one; it will show up here.

editor.title: Edit Template
editor.modeEnforceHint: Formatting is locked — users cannot change element-level styling.
editor.modeOverrideHint: Formatting sets defaults — users can override per-instance.
editor.addElementTitle: Add a custom element (e.g. Sound Effect, Lyric, Insert)

av.inserts: Inserts a two-column Audio/Video body — Video on the left, Audio on the right, one row per shot.
av.noFormatting: It has no formatting of its own. Style the elements that go in its columns instead, and use In AV columns on each of them to say which column offers it.
av.untick: Untick it in the list to keep it out of the element menu; the Format menu’s own AV commands are unaffected.
av.baseTitle: The four AV paragraph types are offered in both columns in every document — only their formatting is a template choice.
av.columnTitle: Which column of a two-column AV body offers this element.

editor.label: Label
editor.newPageOn: Every “{{label}}” begins at the top of a fresh page, on screen and in PDF/Word exports.
editor.newPageOff: This element flows with the rest of the page.

numbering.inline: At the start of the line
numbering.hintOff: Numbers every “{{label}}” in the margin, on screen and in PDF, Word and Final Draft exports.
numbering.summaryWholeShared: {{sample}} … counting through the whole script, in one count with every “{{owner}}”.
numbering.summaryResetShared: {{sample}} … starting again at every {{resets}}, in one count with every “{{owner}}”.
numbering.summaryScene: Plain numbers where there is no scene number to show.
numbering.summaryInline: Shown as the start of the line, even before anything is typed on it.

editor.overrideOn: Users can override formatting for this element type.
editor.overrideOff: All formatting is locked — users cannot change any styling for this element.
editor.selectElement: Select an element from the list to edit its formatting.

select.title: Script Format / Template
select.hint: Choose a script format (screenplay, sitcom, drama, stage play, radio) or a custom formatting template. The template controls element-level formatting rules; for an empty document, choosing a script type also seeds starter content.
select.unreadable: The saved format cannot be read by this version. Its original data is kept when you save. Update OpenDraft to use it; choosing another format replaces the saved definition.
select.libraryNewer: The library version is newer. The local library version is currently in use. Edit Current Format starts from that version; applying this saved copy creates a separate document format.
select.savedNewer: The saved copy is newer. The local library version is currently in use. Edit Current Format starts from that version; applying this saved copy creates a separate document format.
select.libraryInUse: The local library version is currently in use. Edit Current Format starts from that version; applying this saved copy creates a separate document format.
select.savedWithScript: Saved with this script. Editing this format creates a separate document format and leaves your other templates unchanged.
select.copyFailed: Could not save format to your templates.
select.invalidSettings: Invalid template settings. The template was not saved.
select.invalidDocumentSaved: Invalid document format. The template was not saved.
select.invalidDocumentApplied: Invalid document format. The format was not applied.
select.noLongerDefault: No longer the default format for new scripts
